experiment_name: Resume the hash-gated frozen 80-game PURE PPO champion (candidate_ppo_80.pt) for 16 more games under two lower optimizer-LR conditions (A: 1e-4, B: 3e-5, vs. the PPOAgent default 3e-4 every prior run used), identical episode seeds for both conditions, to test whether a lower LR prevents the post-80-game BUY_PROPERTY/ACCEPT_TRADE policy collapse documented in 030/031

algorithm_config.purpose: 030/031 found continuing PPO training past 80 games collapses BUY_PROPERTY (98.5%+ -> 0.0%) and ACCEPT_TRADE (to ~0%) at the default lr=3e-4. This asks whether a lower LR (which should make smaller policy updates per game) avoids or delays that collapse over the SAME 16-game window (80->96 games).
algorithm_config.algorithm_frozen: PPOAgent, ActorNetwork/architecture, PPO hyperparameters other than lr, reward shaping, action space, state pipeline, and the reference submodule were all identical to 027/028/030/031 - only the reference's own unmodified train()/PPOAgent.load/save were called. LR was changed ONLY by mutating the loaded agent's own opt.param_groups[i]['lr'] in the experiment runner (scripts/monopolyzero_lr_ablation_80_resume.py) after PPOAgent.load() restored the checkpoint's Adam optimizer state (moment estimates carried over unchanged) - PPOAgent's own __init__/save/load were never edited.

phase_1_training.method: Each condition independently reloads and hash-verifies the frozen 80-game checkpoint (fresh PPOAgent instance per condition, never sharing state), sets only opt.param_groups lr, then calls the reference's own train(is_ppo=True, hybrid=False, n_games=16, seed=51920) for 16 games (games_trained 80->96). Both conditions use the IDENTICAL seed_arg (51920), so train()'s own per-game episode_seed=seed_arg+absolute_game-1 formula lands on the SAME 16 episode seeds (52000-52015) for A and B - LR is the only difference between the two runs, verified at runtime against the exact logged episode-seed sequence, not merely asserted.
phase_1_training.checkpoints_saved: candidate_ppo_80_lr_ablation_A_lr1e-4_96.pt, candidate_ppo_80_lr_ablation_B_lr3e-5_96.pt - separate files under the same directory as the 80-game champion, neither overwriting it or each other.

phase_2_selection_screen.baseline: three frozen copies of the 80-game champion per game (same hash-gated checkpoint used for both conditions' starting point, loaded fresh and never trained)
phase_2_selection_screen.design: reuses 028/030/031's exact play_one_game/summarize wholesale (deterministic legal-masked argmax for both sides, no new evaluation framework) - one candidate focus seat rotated across all 4 seats per seed, 8 fresh DEV seeds x 4 rotations = 32 games, common set for both candidates
phase_2_selection_screen.seed_pool: fresh DEV range 52100-52107 (8 seeds), registered in scripts/evaluation_protocol.py before this run
phase_2_selection_screen.pre_registered_selection_rule: choose the candidate with the higher win rate on the common selection set; tie-break on higher seed-block mean net worth. If the best candidate's win rate does not exceed 25%, stop and keep the 80-game champion (KILL) - no confirmation run.

phase_3_confirmation.condition: only run if the selected candidate's selection-set win rate exceeded 25%
phase_3_confirmation.design: identical protocol to phase 2, the ONE selected checkpoint only, 20 fresh DEV seeds x 4 rotations = 80 games
phase_3_confirmation.seed_pool: fresh DEV range 52200-52219 (20 seeds), registered before this run

pre_registered_decision_rule.primary_statistic: seed-block bootstrap 95% CI for (selected_candidate_win_rate - 0.25), via evaluation_protocol.seed_block_bootstrap_vs_null (same primary statistic as 028/030/031)
pre_registered_decision_rule.GO: lower bound of the CI is > 0

behavior_diagnostic_only.note: Both LR conditions still collapsed BUY_PROPERTY/ACCEPT_TRADE to ~0% during training, same signature 030/031 documented at the default LR - a lower LR did NOT prevent the behavioral collapse this experiment set out to test.

result: GO on the primary win-rate statistic, but the experiment's actual hypothesis (does a lower LR prevent the post-80-game collapse) is NOT supported - both A (lr=1e-4) and B (lr=3e-5) still collapsed BUY_PROPERTY and ACCEPT_TRADE to essentially 0% of legal opportunities during their 16 training games, the same signature 030/031 documented at the default lr=3e-4. Despite that, the selected candidate (A, lr=1e-4) beat three frozen copies of the 80-game champion on the pre-registered confirmation set: 35/80 = 43.75% win rate, seed-block bootstrap 95% CI for (win_rate - 25%) = [+7.5, +30.0] points, entirely above zero -> GO per the pre-registered rule. Selection-screen win rates for both candidates were individually INCONCLUSIVE by the seed-block bootstrap CI (A: [-3.1,+28.1] pts, B: [-6.3,+21.9] pts) - A was selected only because its raw win rate (37.5%) exceeded the pre-registered 25% selection threshold and was higher than B's (31.25%), per this task's explicit selection rule (raw win rate, not the CI). Net worth and bankruptcy both moved in the candidate's favor (+2788.2 mean net worth, 8.75% vs 37.1% bankruptcy) though neither is the primary statistic. This result should NOT be read as 'lower LR fixes the collapse' - it demonstrates only that a 96-game checkpoint trained this way can still out-play the 80-game champion in real games even while exhibiting the same collapsed BUY_PROPERTY/ACCEPT_TRADE behavior, consistent with 028's earlier finding that this collapse does not necessarily cost win rate on its own.
